title: Tower Crane with Pulley and Cable Physics
prompt:
Create a single-HTML-file Three.js application simulating a tower crane with pulley and cable physics, lifting a loaded cargo.

【Three.js Import (must follow exactly)】
Place in <head>:
<script type="importmap">
{ "imports": {
    "three": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js",
    "three/addons/": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/examples/jsm/"
} }
</script>
Then in <script type="module">:
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { OrbitControls } from 'three/addons/controls/OrbitControls.js';
import { GLTFLoader } from 'three/addons/loaders/GLTFLoader.js';

【Scene Setup】
- Background: gradient sky (light blue #87CEEB to white)
- Camera: perspective, starting at (30, 25, 30) looking at origin
- Lights: one directional (sun, casts shadows), one ambient
- Ground: large flat plane with grid pattern, receives shadows
- OrbitControls with damping enabled

【Crane Structure (procedural geometry)】
Build the crane from basic Three.js geometry:
(1) Vertical mast: tall box (0.8 x 25 x 0.8), positioned at origin, yellow color (#FFD700)
(2) Horizontal jib (boom): box (30 x 0.6 x 0.6), attached at top of mast (y=24), extends in +x direction, yellow
(3) Counter-jib: box (10 x 0.5 x 0.5), extends in -x direction from mast top, with a gray counterweight box at its end
(4) Operator cabin: small box at the mast/jib junction
(5) Trolley: a small gray box (1.0 x 0.4 x 0.8) that slides along the jib. Its x-position is controlled by slider.

【Cable and Pulley Physics (Verlet Integration)】
The cable hangs from the trolley down to the cargo:
- Model cable as a chain of N=20 Verlet particles, connected by distance constraints
- Each segment length = totalCableLength / N
- Top particle is pinned to the trolley position
- Bottom particle is attached to the cargo (robot.glb model)
- Gravity acts on all particles: g = 9.81 m/s^2
- Simple Verlet integration: newPos = 2*currentPos - oldPos + acceleration*dt^2
- Apply distance constraints iteratively (5 constraint-solving passes per frame)
- Render cable as a THREE.Line connecting all particle positions

The cable length determines how far below the trolley the cargo hangs. When cable length is shortened, the cargo is "winched up" because each segment becomes shorter.

【Cargo】
Load robot.glb as the cargo. Scale it to fit about 2 units tall. Attach it to the last particle of the cable chain. The cargo should gently swing as the trolley moves, creating pendulum-like oscillation.

【Wind Effect】
Apply a sinusoidal lateral wind force to all cable particles:
  windForce.x = windStrength * sin(time * 0.5)
  windForce.z = windStrength * cos(time * 0.7)
where windStrength is controllable via slider (range 0 to 5, default 0).

【Crane Rotation】
The entire crane (mast, jib, trolley, cable, cargo) can rotate around the y-axis:
- Press 'A' to rotate left (counterclockwise) at 0.5 rad/s
- Press 'D' to rotate right (clockwise) at 0.5 rad/s
- Rotation causes the cargo to swing outward due to centrifugal effect on the cable

【Controls】
(1) Trolley position slider (id='slider-trolley'): range 2 to 28 (along jib), default 15. Controls trolley x-position along jib.
(2) Cable length slider (id='slider-cable'): range 2 to 20, default 10. Controls total cable length.
(3) Wind strength slider (id='slider-wind'): range 0 to 5, step 0.1, default 0.
(4) Keyboard: 'A'/'D' to rotate crane, 'R' to reset crane rotation to 0.

All sliders should be in a control panel at the bottom of the screen, each with a visible label showing the current value.

【HUD (id='hud')】
Semi-transparent dark panel at top-left:
- id='hud-trolley': Trolley position (1 decimal)
- id='hud-cable': Cable length (1 decimal)
- id='hud-cargo-y': Cargo Y position (2 decimals)
- id='hud-swing': Swing angle from vertical in degrees (1 decimal)
- id='hud-tension': Cable tension at top segment in N (1 decimal)
- id='hud-rotation': Crane rotation in degrees (1 decimal)

【State Management】
Update window.__3D_STATE__ every frame with:
{
  frameCount: number,           // incremented each frame
  trolleyX: number,             // trolley position along jib
  cableLength: number,          // total cable length
  cargoPos: {x, y, z},         // world position of cargo
  cargoSwingAngle: number,      // angle from vertical in radians
  cableTension: number,         // tension force at top cable segment (N)
  craneRotation: number,        // crane y-rotation in radians
  windStrength: number,         // current wind strength
  particleCount: number,        // number of cable particles
  isPaused: boolean,
  simTime: number               // elapsed simulation time in seconds
}

【Physics Constraints】
- Cable tension = mass_cargo * g + centripetal forces from swing
- Cargo Y position should approximate: trolleyY - cableLength (when hanging straight)
- Cable segments must maintain distance constraints (each segment length within 5% of target)
- Pendulum swing should damp naturally due to Verlet integration numerical damping

Output a single HTML file.
physics_constraints: Verlet integration for cable chain with distance constraints. Cable length controls cargo height. Pendulum swing from trolley movement. Wind as lateral sinusoidal force. Centrifugal swing from crane rotation. Constraint-solving with 5 iterations per frame. Cargo Y ~ trolleyY - cableLength when static.
difficulty_analysis: L5: (1) Verlet particle chain with iterative distance constraints is non-trivial; (2) Coupling cargo GLB model to cable end with correct transform; (3) Crane rotation must propagate correctly to trolley, cable, and cargo; (4) Wind force integration into Verlet system; (5) Cable tension calculation from constraint forces; (6) Multiple interacting sliders affecting physics simultaneously; (7) Pendulum dynamics emerge from correct Verlet + constraint implementation.
